Indian Standard
GUIDE FOR EVALUATION OF THERMAL ENDURANCE OF VARNISH .BONDED GLASS FIBRE COVERED RECTANGULAR COPPER CONDUCTORS
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 February 1981, after the draft finalized by the Winding Wires Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 The test method covered in this standard is intended primarily for comparing the thermal endurance of varnish bonded glass fibre lapped or braided rectangular copper conductors in air at atmospheric pressure. In due course similar standard to cover round conductors will be prepared. 0.3 Exposure of some types of varnish bonded glass fibre lapped or braided rectangular conductors to heat in gaseous or liquid environments in the absence of air may give thermal endurance values different from those obtained in air. This fact must be considered when interpreting the results obtained by heating in air in respect to applications where the wire will not be exposed to air in service. 0.4 The method described covers only the evaluation of thermal enduIn due course, other test methods rance by changes in electric strength. to evaluate the changes in other properties will be formulated. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded of7 value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This guide lays down a test procedure for evaluating the useful life of varnish bonded glass fibre lapped or braided rectangular copper conductors of thickness ranging from 0.8 to 5.6 mm and width ranging from 2 to 16 mm. *Rules for rounding off numerical values ( rcuizd),
a

IS : 9778 - 1981 1,~ This standard does not apply to enamelled rectangular copper conductors. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.9 For apply. 2.1 Wire the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall and glass fibre covered

The insulated material -

as received.

2.2 Conductor

The bare metal after removal of the glass covering.

2.3 Increase in Dimensions Due to the Covering - The difference between the thickness over the glass covering and corresponding dimension of the conductor. 3. TEST SPECIMENS 3.1 Preparation of Test Specimens - Samples about 350 mm long of the varnish bonded glass fibre covered conductor shall be bent through 180' on the flat around a mandrel having a diameter 10 times the bare thickness of the conductor. About 10 mm of the insulation is removed from one end of the specimen to facilitate electrical connection. 3.2 Number of Test Specimens - The required is 21 for each exposure temperature. 4. TEMPERATURE EXPOSURE number of test specimens

4.1 In Table 1 the suggested temperature and time of exposure in each cycle are given. A test cycle consists of exposure to high temperature; unless otherwise specified the test shall be carried out within a range of 15" to 35"C, and a relative humidity range of 45 to 75 percent. Before the tests are made, the specimens shall be preconditioned under these atmospheric conditions for a time sufficient to allow the specimens to reach stability. Thermal life values obtained from test specimens subjected to an average of less than 8 or more than 20 cycles at the exposure temperature may not be reliable and should not be used to predict the temperature rating of the insulated conductor. A shorter or longer cycle time than those given in Table 1 may, therefore, be chosen for certain exposure temperature to ensure that the average number of cycles to failure falls within this range. 4.2 It is essential that specimens be aged in an oven that will maintain the average temperature of the specimens within f 2�C ( temperatures lower than or equal to 180�C ) or f 3�C ( temperatures higher than 180�C ) of the desired value. At no time shall the temperature deviate by more than If; 5�C from the average regardless the number of specimens

IS : 9778- 1981 It is also preferable that the change of fresh air in the oven in the oven. be controlled since there is reason to expect that the thermal degradation may be influenced by the fresh air change. There shall be approximately one complete change of fresh air per hour for each square metre of specimen surface. 5. PROOF VOLTAGE TEST

5.1 The test specimens are removed from the oven and cooled to room temperature. To check the condition of the test specimens and to determine the end point of their useful life, each specimen is subjected to a proof voltage test at a frequency of 50 Hz according to the average thickness of the insulation in accordance with Table 2.

6. APPLICATION

OF THE

VOLTAGE

6.1 Each U-shaped specimen shall be placed inside a metal container which shall be filled as shown in Fig. 1 with nickel shots, nickel plated shots or stainless steel ball bearings not more than 2.0 mm in diameter, and maintained in a clean condition by washing it, for example, in thichloroethylene. 6.2 To detect failure, the over current device shall operate when a current The test voltage of 5 mA or more flows through the test voltage circuit. source shall have a capacity to supply a current of 5 mA with a maximum voltage drop of 10 percent. 6.3 The proof voltage shall be applied between the bare conductor and the metal shots ( which are earthed ), for a period of 1 minute as shown in Fig. 1. 6.4 Care shall be taken in all cases to avoid mechanical damage of the test specimens. The specimens that fail the test voltage are discarded and the remaining ones are returned to the oven for the next cycle of temperature exposure,

7. CALCULATION 7.1 The cycles of temperature exposure, cooling and application of test voltage are continued until 11 specimens have failed at each exposure temperature. 7.2 The median life of specimens at each ageing temperature is calculated by taking the failure time of the eleventh specimen, that is, the exposure

7

IS t 9778 - 1981
time in hours taken to cause 11 specimen of cycle in hours.

\ to fail minus half the duration

7.3 The same is repeated at other exposure temperatures. The test specimens are subjected to 4 exposure temperatures which lie 20�C apart at the initial two temperature ranges of three exposures and the last two highest temperatures shall be at 10�C apart. It is recommended that the lowest ageing temperature should be 20�C above the anticipated temperature index for the varnish bonded glass fibre lapped or braided rectangular copper conductors. The life-temperature characteristic is plotted on a graph paper; the failure times are plotted with a logarithmic scale on the ordinate and the reciprocal of the absolute temperature as the abscissa. The data so obtained may not permit accurate extrapolation in which case a line of best fit may be drawn statistically, and extrapolated to 20 000 hours. In the median life procedure, if median life of less than 100 hours is obtained at the highest exposure temperature, it should be disregarded. A statistical analysis of the thermal endurance test results is given in Appendix A.
